{{Quote|Cliegg Lars. Shmi is my wife.|Cliegg Lars introduces himself to Anakin Skywalker, his step-son|<ref name="Episode II" />}}
'''Cliegg Lars''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[moisture farmer]] from the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. He lived and worked on a [[Lars homestead|family farm]] he inherited from his parents with his son from his [[Aika Lars|first marriage]], [[Owen Lars]], and Owen's girlfriend [[Beru Whitesun Lars|Beru Whitesun]]. Though the [[Lars family]] was content with their simple lives, they became involved with the [[White Suns]] liberation movement, which helped free Tatooine's [[Slavery|slaves]]. Because of his work with the movement, Cliegg met his future wife, [[Shmi Skywalker Lars]]. Through his [[marriage]] to her, Cliegg would be the step-father of [[Anakin Skywalker]] and the step-grandfather of [[Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]].

Cliegg won Shmi's freedom in a [[Gambling|bet]] with her enslaver, [[Watto]], and the two moved to the Lars homestead, where they married and lived happily as moisture farmers. Using a deprogramming device the family had designed to remove Shmi's [[transmitter chip]], the Larses secretly helped emancipate escaped slaves. One day, however, Shmi was captured by a band of [[Tusken Raider]]s. Cliegg organized a [[Cliegg Lars' quadrille|posse]] to rescue her, but the attempt failed, and he lost his right leg in the process. As he mourned her, Cliegg was visited by her son, Anakin Skywalker, who led his own [[Mission to rescue Shmi Skywalker Lars|rescue mission]], but the boy returned only with her corpse. Cliegg never recovered from the incident and [[Death|died]] shortly after. He was [[Burial|buried]] alongside Shmi on the farm, which was bequeathed to Owen and Beru.

==Biography==
===A tragic youth===
[[File:YetAnotherTatooineSunset.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Cliegg Lars built the Lars family homestead, where his family worked as moisture farmers.]]
Cliegg Lars was [[Reproduction|born]] to [[Lef Lars|Lef]] and [[Gredda Lars]] on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] in [[the galaxy]]'s [[Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="Complete Locations" /> Despite the arid conditions of Tatooine and the danger posed to settlers by the native [[Tusken Raider]] tribes,<ref name="Lars Farm DB">{{Databank|lars-moisture-farm|Lars Moisture Farm}}</ref> the small and humble Lars family, which included Cliegg's brother [[Edern Lars|Edern]],<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> became pioneers of the [[Great Chott salt flat]], where they operated a [[Lars homestead|moisture farm]] on the outskirts of a settlement known as [[Anchorhead]].<ref name="Lars Farm DB" /> Cliegg helped found and build the underground homestead, and the Lars family made their living<ref name="Complete Locations" /> harvesting [[water]] from the atmosphere by employing the use of dozens of [[moisture vaporator]]s.<ref name="100Objects">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> Because the water harvests rarely supplied the Larses with quantities sufficient enough to sell for profit, the family kept the water for themselves to sustain their [[Hydroponics|hydroponic]] [[garden]]s instead.<ref name="Complete Locations" /> Tragedy would strike the Lars family when Edern suffered an untimely [[death]]<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion" /> at the age of fourteen when he lost control of the family's [[V-35 Courier]] [[landspeeder]].<ref name="Complete Locations" />

Over time, Edern was followed in death by Lef and Gredda,<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion" /> and all three were [[Burial|buried]] on the family's property.<ref name="Complete Locations" /> Cliegg, the last surviving member of his immediate family, decided to leave the moisture farm behind.<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion" /> Still a young man, Cliegg wanted to experience life on a bustling [[Core Worlds|Core World]] and departed Tatooine to explore the galaxy. In the galactic Core, Cliegg met a woman named Aika, and the two fell in love, [[Marriage|married]], and parented a son together, Owen.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Despite the brief reprieve, Aika died when Owen was still very young, leading Cliegg to decide to return to his homeworld with his son. As Owen grew up, he became a diligent farmhand and helped his father operate the moisture farm. As a young adult, Owen developed a relationship with a local girl named [[Beru Whitesun Lars|Beru Whitesun]], who became his girlfriend, and the Lars family grew when she moved into the homestead.<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion" />

===A new chance at happiness===
====The White Suns====
{{Quote|You think there are people working against slavery on Tatooine?|Galactic Republic Senator Padmé Amidala on the White Suns movement|<ref name="Queen's Shadow">''[[Queen's Shadow]]''</ref>}}
In the twilight years of the [[Republic Era]],<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion" /> the Lars family began aiding the [[White Suns]], a liberation movement established to organize the emancipation of [[Slavery|enslaved]] beings on Tatooine. It was by chance that the Larses would be introduced to [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]], who would go on to become an integral part of their family. While on a supply run in the [[city]] of [[Mos Espa]], Beru's portable navigator unit malfunctioned, and at the recommendation of a merchant she had been bartering with, she went to Skywalker's residence<ref name="Queen's Hope">''[[Queen's Hope]]''</ref> in the [[Slave Quarters Row]]<ref name="Complete Locations" /> to have it fixed for cheap. When Beru returned to the Lars homestead, she told Cliegg and Owen of Shmi's talent for tinkering with machines, which soon became of interest to the White Suns. On behalf of the White Suns, Cliegg went to meet with Shmi, and he, too, became interested in her following their first conversation. Over the following [[Standard week|weeks]], Shmi told Cliegg, Owen, and Beru about her enslaver, the [[Toydarian]] junk dealer [[Watto]], such as how he cheated to avoid the White Suns.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

[[File:Shmi_Skywalker_Databank.png|thumb|right|250px|Through his work with the White Suns liberation movement, Cliegg Lars was introduced to Shmi Skywalker, who would become his second wife.]]
To give Shmi time away from serving Watto, Cliegg hired her out from the junk dealer, ostensibly to tune his moisture vaporators. They developed a liking for one another and, in their time spent together, grew close. Though Shmi spent much of her time on the farm with Cliegg, she also set about working with Beru to build a tracking device that could be used to locate the [[transmitter chip]]s planted in those enslaved on Tatooine.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> Around [[27 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> the day finally came for Cliegg to make his move and emancipate Shmi from Watto's ownership. Armed with Shmi's information about Watto's weaknesses and [[gambling]] tendencies, Cliegg lured Watto into a game where she was the promised prize. Lars won the game and,<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> after settling the reward with Watto,<ref name="Timelines" /> quickly brought Shmi<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> and her [[protocol droid]], [[C-3PO]],<ref name="Episode II" /> away from Mos Espa and to the boundaries of his farm, setting her free. Though Shmi was no longer enslaved, her transmitter chip remained somewhere in her body.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

Over the next three [[Standard month|months]], the Larses and Skywalker worked tirelessly to complete a functioning deprogrammer device to remove Shmi's chip. The work was tedious, and it was only because of Cliegg's technical ownership of her that Shmi could volunteer to have the device tested on her; had she still been under the control of Watto or another enslaver, a monitoring device would notify them that the chip was being tampered with. Since the monitor connected to Shmi's chip belonged to Cliegg, someone who cared about her, the Larses knew Shmi would be unharmed if they removed her chip, but an enslaved person taken in by the White Suns would not have the luxury of time. Though Cliegg, Beru, and Owen continued to fret over the situation, Shmi remained positive, in part because her son, [[Anakin Skywalker|Anakin]], who had once been Watto's slave but was taken in by the [[Jedi Order]], had always wanted to build a deprogrammer. At the end of the three months, Shmi and Beru finished the device and had only to test it once more.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

Cliegg couldn't bear to watch the procedure again, and Owen took him to the other side of the homestead to keep him distracted. While Cliegg and Owen waited, Beru successfully located Shmi's chip, which was fused to her lower spine. Knowing that they would have only a short window before the monitoring device discovered that the chip was being disturbed, Beru made quick and clean cuts into Shmi's skin and removed the chip, deactivating it. The experiment was successful, leading Cliegg, Owen, Beru, and Shmi to use the deprogrammer on escaped slaves they took in. The Lars homestead became an important stopping point of the underground White Suns, where fugitive slaves had their chips removed. The procedure did not always work, and some of those they tried helping died during the chip's removal, but the Larses remained devoted to their cause, and Shmi worked endlessly to improve the device.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

====Losing Shmi====
{{Quote|Thirty of us went out after her. Four of us came back. I'd be with them, but… after I lost my leg I just couldn't ride anymore, until I heal. I don't want to give up on her, but she's been gone a month. There's little hope she's lasted this long.|Cliegg Lars tells Anakin Skywalker about his mother|<ref name="Episode II" />}}
Having grown close in the time they knew each other,<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> Cliegg and Shmi married, and Shmi adopted his surname.<ref name="Cliegg Databank">{{Databank|cliegg-lars|Cliegg Lars}}</ref> With their marriage, the Lars and Skywalker families officially blended.<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion" /> Cliegg, Shmi, Owen, and Beru lived quiet lives on their homestead, where they survived against the harsh desert together while continuing their anti-slavery work.<ref name="Cliegg Databank" /> Shmi brought happiness into the Lars family, and she became a bright center and indispensable part of their family unit.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> Though she was greatly content with her marriage to Cliegg and emancipated life on the farm, Shmi spent many nights worrying about Anakin and his well-being.<ref name="Ultimate SW" /> After existing as an island of familial warmth amidst the vast desert wastelands, tragedy soon struck the Larses.<ref name="Cliegg Databank" /> In [[22 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Shmi was picking mushrooms off the moisture vaporators when, just before dawn, a Tusken hunting party arrived and took her captive. Cliegg immediately investigated her disappearance, concluding she had been halfway home when the Tuskens took her.<ref name="Episode II" />

[[File:AnakinClieggOwen-AotC.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Cliegg tells Anakin Skywalker the story of his failed attempt to rescue Shmi.]]
Cliegg assembled a [[Cliegg Lars' quadrille|quadrille]] of thirty moisture farmers, including himself,<ref name="Episode II" /> and prepared to take on the Tusken tribe he believed had kidnapped his wife.<ref name="100Objects" /> Despite their brave effort to rescue Shmi, the farmers were outmatched by the Tusken Raiders and were slaughtered. Of the thirty posse members,<ref name="Episode II" /> only four survived the counter-raid, including Cliegg. Although Cliegg managed to survive the violent attack, his right leg had been hacked off at the knee. Rather than incur the expense of a cybernetic prosthesis for his lost leg, Lars took to using a [[repulsorlift chair]], which he found more practical.<ref name="100Objects" /> Over the next month, Cliegg lost hope and believed that Shmi was no longer alive. While he, Owen, and Beru mourned their loss, the farm was visited by Anakin Skywalker, who had been haunted by dreams of his mother in agony. Skywalker arrived with [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], who was under his protection. Upon their arrival, C-3PO led them into the homestead.<ref name="Episode II" />

While Skywalker and Amidala greeted Owen and Beru, Cliegg entered the room and introduced himself to Anakin as Shmi's husband, then invited him inside to discuss what had happened. In the dining room, Beru served everyone drinks while Cliegg informed his stepson of Shmi's disappearance and his failed rescue attempt. Lars was pessimistic that Shmi was still alive, but an emotional Anakin got up from the table. Owen asked where he was going, and the Jedi Knight replied that he was going to find his mother. Cliegg implored him to accept that Shmi was dead, but Skywalker was adamant and left the farm in the evening, leaving Senator Amidala in the care of the Larses. During the night, Anakin was able to track down the Tusken Raiders' [[Tusken Raider camp|camp]], and he found his mother, emaciated and bound but still alive. Though Anakin tried to escape with her, she died in his arms, after which he massacred the entire Tusken tribe, including women and children, in a fit of fury.<ref name="Episode II" />

====Joining his wife====
{{Quote|I know wherever you are, it's become a better place. You were the most loving partner a man could ever have. Good-bye, my darling wife, and thank you.|Cliegg Lars, at Shmi's funeral|<ref name="Episode II" />}}
[[File:Lars_family.png|thumb|right|250px|C-3PO, Padmé Amidala, Anakin Skywalker, Beru, Owen, and Cliegg at Shmi's funeral.]]
The next morning, Anakin returned to the Lars homestead with Shmi's corpse. The Larses placed her body in a coffin,<ref name="Darth Vader 1">[[Darth Vader (2020) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 1]]</ref> and she was buried next to Cliegg's parents and brother.<ref name="Complete Locations" /> [[Funeral of Shmi Skywalker Lars|A small funeral service]] was held later that day,<ref name="Episode II" /> and Cliegg briefly spoke his last respects.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> Anakin too spoke, but instead of memorializing Shmi, he swore never to allow himself to fail anyone else as he had failed her. The funeral was interrupted by Anakin and Padmé's droid, [[R2-D2]], who informed them that he had received a message for them.<ref name="Episode II" /> The visitors remained at the farm for just a short while longer,<ref name="BWL">{{StoryCite|story=Beru Whitesun Lars (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref> and just as soon as they had arrived, Skywalker and Amidala left the Lars family alone once more.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

Cliegg was bereft at the loss of Shmi, while Owen barely contained his anger as well. Beru remained steadfast and continued the family's work with the White Suns even as Cliegg and Owen dealt with the loss.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> After some time, Cliegg was determined to continue the life he had worked hard to create on Tatooine<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and began working to make the Lars homestead an oasis of security in the desert,<ref name="Cliegg Databank" /> but he quickly began to fade as the tragedy continued to weigh him down heavily. The once-strong man became weak even as time passed since Shmi's death,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and he died from the wounds he received from the Tuskens<ref name="Ultimate SW" /> and of a broken heart not long after her death.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Cliegg's body was, like Shmi's, placed in a coffin and buried next to hers. The Lars homestead was bequeathed to Owen and Beru,<ref name="Darth Vader 1" /> who married and sought to continue the family's traditions.<ref name="Owen SWE">{{SWE|characters|owenlars|Owen Lars}}</ref>

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Wait a moment...I'm detecting a few rectangular cuboids two meters below the surface...yes, there we go! Cliegg Lars' and Shmi's graves must be down below. Owen and Beru must have removed the headstones. Protecting the boy, probably.|ZED-6-7, discovering Cliegg and Shmi's unmarked graves|<ref name="Darth Vader 1" />}}
[[File:VaderAndZED67OnTatooine-2020DarthVader1.jpg|thumb|left|220px|During a visit to the abandoned Lars homestead, Darth Vader, formerly Anakin Skywalker, and the droid ZED-6-7 discovered the graves of Cliegg and Shmi Lars.]]
Owen and Beru worked hard to maintain the farm<ref name="Owen SWE">{{SWE|characters|owenlars|Owen Lars}}</ref> that Cliegg had founded.<ref name="Complete Locations" /> At the end of the [[Clone Wars]], Owen and Beru were made the guardians of [[Luke Skywalker]], Anakin's son. Owen and Beru were entrusted by [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Anakin's former teacher, to keep Luke safe and hidden from his father, who had turned to the [[dark side of the Force]] and become Darth Vader amid the rise of the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> As a measure of keeping Luke safe, the headstones above Cliegg and Shmi's graves were sandblasted. Early in his stay on Tatooine to watch over Luke, Kenobi, ventured to Shmi's grave to apologize for Anakin's downfall. Though he had never known her, he felt guilt that he and the Jedi never released her from slavery as they did for Anakin, and reflected to himself that it was only Cliegg's love for her that saved her from bondage.<ref name="Ahsoka">[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']]</ref>

Obi-Wan often visited the burial site and sometimes left toys there for the young boy.<ref name="Time of Death">{{StoryCite|story=Time of Death|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref> At some point, Owen and Beru went one step further and removed all the headstones from the Lars property, leaving Cliegg's grave,<ref name="Darth Vader 1" /> as well as those of his parents, brother,<ref name="Complete Locations" /> and second wife unmarked.<ref name="Darth Vader 1" /> The Lars homestead was destroyed<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> in [[1 BBY]]<ref name="IV Date">{{FilmDate|IV|1}}</ref> when, after unknowingly taking in two fugitive droids, [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]], Owen and Beru were executed by Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s, and the farm was burned. Luke, who had been away from the farm at the time, joined Obi-Wan Kenobi on a mission away from Tatooine after their murders and became a hero in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="ANH" /> The farm was left abandoned after Luke left, and it became a target for Tusken Raiders, who damaged what was left of the former homestead despite the absence of any inhabitants.<ref name="Darth Vader 1" />

Years later, Darth Vader, after learning of Luke's existence and [[Duel on Cloud City|confronting him]], returned to the homestead to learn more about his son. Vader was accompanied by a [[forensics droid]], [[ZED-6-7]], who listed off the former residents of the abandoned farm, including Cliegg and Shmi. Vader was haunted by his memories of his mother's death and his visit to the farm. ZED later located the coffins belonging to Cliegg and Shmi, which he detected were two meters below the surface. ZED speculated that Owen and Beru had removed the headstones, and his further scans found no evidence of Cliegg's son or daughter-in-law's remains. Vader and ZED left shortly after.<ref name="Darth Vader 1" /> The farm built by Cliegg Lars<ref name="Complete Locations" /> was left in its ruined state and,<ref name="Darth Vader 1" /> by [[35 ABY]],<ref name="Date 35">{{FilmDate|IX}}</ref> had begun to disappear under the sands of Tatooine.<ref name="TROS">{{Film|IX}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Your mother's dead, son. Accept it.|Cliegg Lars tells Anakin Skywalker to accept his mother's death|<ref name="Episode II" />}}
[[File:ClieggLarsDetail-SWE.png|thumb|right|170px|Lars used a power chair after losing his right leg trying to rescue Shmi from Tusken Raiders.]]
Cliegg Lars was a [[human]] male who stood at 1.83 [[meter]]s, or 6 [[Foot|feet]]. He had [[Color|blue]] [[eye]]s, light skin, and blond [[hair]],<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> which by the time of Shmi's kidnapping was graying on the sides.<ref name="Episode II" /> Though a modest man content with his quiet and peaceful life as a moisture farmer on Tatooine,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> Cliegg had a yearning to experience a more bustling place to live in his youth. His life, however, was one marked by tragic losses. The death of his first wife, Aika, dashed Cliegg's dreams of a life away from Tatooine,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and he also lived through the deaths of his brother and parents.<ref name="Complete Locations" /> Cliegg was a tough and strong-willed individual,<ref name="Ultimate SW" /> but he was also a good-hearted<ref name="Cliegg Databank" /> and humorous person, and he used his sense of humor to make his second wife, Shmi Skywalker, laugh even in dire situations.<ref name="Queen's Hope" />

When Cliegg and Shmi married, they happily formed a family unit with Owen and Beru, and lived in peace on the Lars homestead.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> Cliegg was happy to be able to share his life with as good a person as Shmi was.<ref name="SWCT">{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Cliegg Lars - Moisture Farmer}}</ref> Altogether, the Larses dared to aid in the emancipation of enslaved persons in secret and used their land as a place for escaped slaves to seek help.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> Though Cliegg was able to see his family create a warm and loving environment,<ref name="Cliegg Databank" /> their happiness was shattered by Shmi's kidnapping and death.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> The kind Cliegg<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> became angry and spiteful towards the Tusken Raiders for what they did to her, and he saw them as nothing more than vicious animals.<ref name="Episode II" /> Cliegg never recovered from the loss, and though he attempted to accept her death, move on, and continue his life's work,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> he grew weaker without her and succumbed to his sadness, becoming a shell of the man he once was and eventually dying as such.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

==Equipment==
Cliegg Lars wore weather-worn work [[Clothing|clothes]], which included a light brown tunic and undershirt, gray pants, and a sleeveless gray duster [[Jacket|coat]]. He also wore a gear harness that was wrapped around his midriff and slung over his left shoulder.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> After losing his right leg and injuring the other in his failed mission to rescue Shmi, Cliegg was forced to use a repulsorlift-powered chair to mobilize.<ref name="Episode II" /> Although Lars was content with the repulsorlift chair's inexpensive practicality, the mobility device was uncomfortable and the seat could not be adjusted, and the only semblance of luxury it offered was a footrest for his remaining leg.<ref name="100Objects" />

==Behind the scenes==
Cliegg Lars first appeared in the second film in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]], [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']],<ref name="Episode II" /> which was released on [[May 16]], [[2002]].<ref name="Season 2 Directors">{{ThisWeek|u0Z7i0LnXOg|Mandalorian Season 2 Directors, We Celebrate a Birthday, and More!|sw_url=video/mandalorian-season-2-directors-we-celebrate-a-birthday-and-more}}</ref> The name Cliegg, or variations of it, had existed since the earliest screenplay drafts of the [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|original Star Wars]]. One rough draft from [[1974]] featured a young blonde [[Alderaanian]] character named Cliegg Whitesun.<ref name="Cliegg DB">{{DB|character|cliegglars|Lars, Cliegg}}</ref>

In ''Attack of the Clones'', Lars was portrayed by [[Jack Thompson]]. During shooting, Thompson wore a blue sock to facilitate the digital removal of his leg by [[Industrial Light & Magic|Industrial Light and Magic]].<ref name="Cliegg DB" />
